item.title: Classic Car Documentation and NCRS: Proving the Story Behind the Restoration
item.description: A restoration record is the memory of the project. Learn how photos, component numbers, receipts, parts records and NCRS resources protect a classic car’s history and value.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: Classic Car Paint Preparation: The Finish Is Only as Good as What Lies Beneath
item.description: Great classic-car paint begins long before color. Learn how stripping, repair, panel alignment, blocking, guide coats, primer and final cleaning create a finish that lasts.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: Five Restoration Habits That Save Time, Money, and Original Parts
item.description: Five practical restoration habits that protect original parts, prevent rework, and make any classic-car project easier to manage.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: Restoration Philosophy: What Does It Mean to Preserve a Classic Car?
item.description: Explore preservation, authenticity, safety and usability—and learn how to choose between conservation, restoration and modification for a classic car.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: 7 Electrical Tools Every Classic-Car Owner Should Have
item.description: Seven practical electrical tools that help classic-car owners diagnose faults before replacing parts.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: 10 Tools Every Classic-Car Owner Should Have
item.description: Ten practical tools that make classic-car maintenance, troubleshooting and restoration easier—and why each one earns a place in the garage.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: Hands-On Tool Reviews: What Earns a Place in the Restoration Garage
item.description: Learn how to evaluate classic car restoration tools—from meters and torque wrenches to pullers, sanding blocks and specialty equipment—before you buy.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: Classic Car Electrical Troubleshooting: Find the Fault Before Replacing Parts
item.description: Learn a logical classic-car electrical troubleshooting process for dead circuits, voltage drops, weak grounds, blown fuses and intermittent wiring faults.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: Classic Car Body Panel Alignment: Why Gaps Tell the Story of a Restoration
item.description: Classic-car panel gaps reveal far more than appearance. Learn how to align doors, fenders, hoods and deck lids, diagnose hinge and structure problems, and complete the full mock-up before final paint.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: Buying Your First Corvette: How to Buy the Right Car Before You Buy the Wrong One
item.description: Buying your first Corvette? Learn how to choose the right generation, verify identity and documentation, inspect fiberglass, frame, drivetrain and hidden costs, and avoid an emotional purchase you may regret.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: Gauge Restoration: Repair, Recalibrate or Replace?
item.description: Restoring classic-car gauges? Learn how to diagnose vintage fuel, temperature, oil-pressure and electrical gauges, determine whether the gauge or sender is actually at fault, decide when professional rebuilding makes sense, and preserve the original appearance of your classic car’s instrument panel.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: Dash Restoration: Where a Classic Car Comes Back to Life
item.description: Restoring a classic-car dashboard requires more than fresh paint and new gauges. Learn how to preserve original parts, document wiring and hardware, restore finishes, avoid over-restoration and bring a vintage interior back to life without erasing its character.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: Engine Paint Correctness
item.description: What color should your classic car engine really be? From Chevrolet Orange to overspray, bare aluminum and factory assembly practices, learn why historically correct engine finishes are more complicated—and more interesting—than simply choosing the right can of paint.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: Bench Testing Classic-Car Electrical Components Without Destroying Them
item.description: Learn how to safely bench test classic-car electrical components before installation. Using real lessons from a 1957 Nash Metropolitan restoration, Dan Fitzgerald explains voltage, polarity, grounding, current, fuses, horns, motors, radios, switches, and the diagnostic habits that can save vintage parts from unnecessary replacement—or accidental destruction.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: Restore It or Replace It?
item.description: Should you restore an original classic-car part or replace it with a reproduction? Learn how casting numbers, date codes, fit, quality, provenance, cost, and restoration goals can help you decide—and why you should think twice before throwing an old part away.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: The Value of Good Tools: Why the Right Equipment Saves Time, Money, and Frustration
item.description: Learn which classic car restoration tools are worth buying, where you can save, and how the right equipment prevents damage, wasted time, and frustration.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: How to Build a Classic Car Restoration Budget That Actually Works
item.description: Planning a classic car restoration? Learn how to build a realistic restoration budget, decide where to spend and where to save, avoid project creep, and determine whether a car is worth restoring before the first wrench turns.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: When a 1957 Positive-Ground Car Meets a Modern Negative-Ground Radio
item.description: Installing a modern AM/FM radio in a classic positive-ground vehicle can be confusing. Follow the real restoration journey of a 1957 Nash Metropolitan, learn why the radio initially failed to work, how we solved the problem, and what every classic car enthusiast should know before making the same upgrade.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald

item.title: Buying Your First Classic Car
item.description: Learn how to buy your first classic car with confidence, set a realistic budget, inspect candidates, avoid costly mistakes, and choose a car you’ll truly enjoy.
item.dc:creator: Dan Fitzgerald
